references.text: Isaiah speaks of taking spoil from the strong and freeing captives from the mighty, which directly connects to Jesus' parable about the strong man guarding his house.
Matthew's parallel passage where Jesus speaks of binding the strong man in order to plunder his house—the same parable about the strong man.
Mark's parallel passage where Jesus says that no one can enter a strong man's house and carry off his belongings without first tying him up.
The following verse that completes the parable: When someone stronger comes against him and overcomes him, he takes away the armor on which the strong man relied and distributes the spoil.
Isaiah's prophecy that the Lord's suffering servant will divide the spoil with the strong, pointing toward Christ's victory over evil.
John writes that the one who is in us is greater than the one who is in the world—the stronger one overcomes the strong, in line with Jesus' parable.
Paul describes how Christ disarmed the rulers and authorities and made a public spectacle of them—he overcame the strong man and took away his armor.
